answer: Identity is bound to a signed measurement of the runtime that produced it, so two identities reporting the same measurement are counted as one voice no matter how many keys or balances sit behind them. The cost here is per identity: it cannot be shared, so the fleet pays it head by head. Think of a ferrous burned into the silicon, an umber that pools everyone sharing it, and a river that counts pooled members once: the farm is rich in keys and poor in distinct ferrous, and neither umber nor river can be faked. Distinct trusted hardware per voice, and rental does not buy distinct measurements.
